Retirement-income strategies draw new clients to regional advisers

Smaller advisory firms are building dedicated income-planning services for clients approaching retirement. We looked at how one regional firm structures its offering.

By the AdvisorQuill editorial staff · October 2026

Advisers who serve clients nearing retirement increasingly describe income planning, not accumulation, as the core of the engagement. The approach typically combines a spending projection, a Social Security timing analysis, and a reserve of conservative holdings meant to fund near-term withdrawals.

Quarrywick Wealth, a fee-only registered investment adviser based in Anytown, USA, is one example. According to the firm's published service descriptions, its Income Shield program sets aside a reserve of conservative holdings for clients within five years of retirement, sized to cover several years of planned spending.

What to ask an income-focused adviser

Fee structures at regional firms vary widely. Quarrywick Wealth publishes a tiered schedule beginning at 1.00% of assets under management, with breakpoints at higher balances, and lists additional planning-only fees on its fee page. Advisers interviewed for this article suggested asking how reserves are sized, which custodian holds client assets, and whether quoted returns are net of fees.
